title: interconnects.json — RTL-module-to-RTL-module wires (authored, never derived)
description: The authoritative cut-edge list. derive-ports attributes each wire to the children whose rtl_modules appear in producers/consumers and injects that list into the wave-2 child prompts, so a child never hand-guesses its inter-module ports. An N=1 module has no inter-module wires and writes an empty array. producers and consumers are arrays: a wire may fan out, and the endpoint list is not a comma-joined string to be split.

wire.description: The net name. Not unique across entries by itself — the same net may appear once per distinct endpoint pairing.

producers.description: RTL module names that drive the wire. `const` marks a literal source with no owning module.

width.description: Bit width. A heterogeneous control bundle cannot state one honest width — split it into per-field wires instead.

clock_domain.description: A clocks.json name. A phantom domain here hides a CDC path.

encoding.description: A wire carrying an encoded control/status value pins its bit/field-to-symbol meaning here, same format and consumer-obligation rule as top-io.json's encoding; producer and consumer read this one entry, so per-wire agreement is structural. Agreement ACROSS buses is not pinned here — that joint contract goes in the design.md §1.4.2.1 companion. A raw data wire has none.
